sections.title: Tree and leaves
sections.text: Populus nigra, black poplar, is a large deciduous tree that may reach about 30 m. Its alternate, broadly diamond-shaped to triangular leaves are usually 5–11 cm long and finely toothed.

sections.title: Flowers and seeds
sections.text: Male and female flowers grow on separate trees. The reddish male catkins are about 3–5 cm long; the female catkins are longer, about 10–15 cm. Capsules release seeds carried in cottony hairs.

sections.title: Comparison
sections.text: It differs from the European aspen, P. tremula, in its more angular leaves and longer female catkins.
